The tool should emit progress notifications while waiting, or cap its default/max timeout below the client idle limit; shell 'ddflow wait --timeout 570' works.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bfc43dae5b9: ddflow_wait via MCP with timeout=1800 sent no response or progress for 1800s and the client aborted it (MCP tool idle timeout). The tool should emit progress notifications while waiting, or cap its default/max timeout below the client idle limit; shell 'ddflow wait --timeout 570' works.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfc43dae5b9 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfc43dae5b9 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bfc43dae5b9: MCP ddflow_wait gives no progress; client aborts at 1800s idle

chunk_findings.detail: The manual gives two mutually exclusive startup orders. Line 11 says "Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else," while line 25 says that if several agents or subagents are present, "call `ddflow_identify` first." In the multi-agent case, following line 11 causes the exact failure the manual itself describes at lines 28-30: identity is derived from the shared worktree, the agents merge into a single identity, `ddflow_brief` answers with someone else's task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself. An agent in that environment may claim or edit the wrong item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:11 and :25

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs that `ddflow_brief` "replaces reading this project's rule and lesson files — do not read those instead," but `ddflow_brief` is described as returning decisions that govern the files about to be touched and lessons ranked for the current task. The manual never restates the global advisory r-ddflow-self-assessment (assess ddflow at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction). An agent that obeys the manual's prohibition on reading the rule files has no remaining source for that required self-assessment and will omit it. This violates the advisory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:13-15 [r-ddflow-self-assessment]

chunk_findings.detail: The compact text “One of several agents: `ddflow_identify` first, or `as_agent` on every call” makes `ddflow_identify` first an acceptable option on the stateless `2026-07-28` revision. On that revision there is no initialize connection, so `ddflow_identify` persists nothing; the old instructions explicitly said to name yourself on every call via `as_agent` or `_meta`. Given multiple agents in one worktree on that revision, an agent calls `ddflow_identify` once and stops; unlabeled later calls are derived from the working tree, identities merge, `ddflow_brief` can answer with someone else’s task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself and pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md:44

chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional loop “`ddflow_merge`, `ddflow_complete`” removes the PR integration branch. In a project with `[flow].integration = "pr"`, `ddflow_merge` opens the pull request, parks the item IN REVIEW, and releases the lease; the original contract said “do not wait and do not `ddflow_complete` it — take the next item.” The new charter tells that agent to call `ddflow_complete` on a parked item, producing a refusal/confusing loop exactly in the PR-flow case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md:44

chunk_findings.detail: The "byte cap" is checked with `len(text)`, which counts Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes. The previous `mcp_instructions` pipeline line contained `" implement ·"` (U+00B7), so non-ASCII characters can make `len(text) <= 1500` while `len(text.encode()) > 1500`; the same issue is in the unadopted assertion at line 50 and the SessionStart assertion at line 75. Thus the cap this test is meant to enforce is not actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: After setting `gates.task_pipeline` to `implement,unit_tests,merge`, the test locates the `Gates:` line and only asserts that `rubber_duck` is absent. It no longer asserts that the configured gates appear, so a broken `_instructions` output such as `Gates: research · critic` passes both assertions. The test named `test_the_pipeline_shown_is_the_project_s_own` would fail to catch a regression that renders a different pipeline.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_instructions.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: The pointer assertion is `assert "topic=manual" in _instructions(repo) or "manual" in _instructions(repo)`. Since `"manual"` is a substring of `"topic=manual"`, the second clause makes the first redundant and allows any mention of the word "manual" to satisfy the check. An instructions text like `"This is not a manual; call ddflow_help."` passes even though it never names the `manual` topic, so the test does not prove the charter points at the manual.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The manual asserts “A plain `ddflow_review` of a gate with a recorded review is a full re-review”, but the same parenthetical states `full=true` is needed when `[review].delta_default` is on—meaning a plain `ddflow_review` is not a full re-review in that configuration. Under `[review].delta_default = true`, an agent following the broad statement will call plain `ddflow_review` expecting the whole diff; the tool actually performs a delta review only (full requires `full=true`), so the full diff is never re-reviewed and a gate can pass with unreviewed changes. The sentence must be qualified: plain is full only when `delta_default` is off; when it is on, plain is delta and `full=true` is required for a full review.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:88-90

chunk_findings.detail: The cap is measured with `len(text.encode())`, which counts UTF-8 bytes, while the project cap is specified in characters (`<=1.5K chars`, `CHARTER_MAX_CHARS`). Given an adopted charter of 1500 characters containing one non-ASCII character such as `—` (3 UTF-8 bytes), line 45 reports `1502 bytes > 1500` and fails even though the character cap is met. The same `.encode()` byte measurement is reused at lines 53 and 85, so valid non-ASCII framing would be incorrectly rejected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The SessionStart contract in the intent includes “where to fetch more” (`ddflow_recall`/`ddflow_help`), but this test only asserts that `"claim"`, `"operator"`, `"unavailable"`, and `"ddflow_brief"` appear in `SESSION_START_HEADER + SESSION_START_FOOTER`. A framing such as `"ddflow_brief first. claim before edit. ask the operator. unavailable never passed."` with an empty footer would pass the test even though it omits the fetch-more instruction, so the test does not enforce the contract it is named for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:85

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not exercise the behavior it is replacing. It calls `_instruction_vars(repo)`, then forcibly overrides `vars_["actionable_companions"] = []` before rendering, so it never verifies how `_instruction_vars` decides that no companion needs action. The removed test `test_a_registered_companion_is_not_listed_as_missing` actually registered `context7` and checked the real served instructions omitted it. Concrete missing input: a repository where `context7` is registered but `_instruction_vars` still returns it in `actionable_companions` — the served instructions would still say “not wired up”, yet this test passes because the hand-set `[]` hides the bug. The regression guard is lost.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_instructions.py: test_the_companion_line_is_only_said_when_one_needs_action

chunk_findings.detail: The first step still says “Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else” while in the same rewritten sentence says, for one of several agents/subagents, “name yourself first.” Those are two different first actions, and the absolute “before anything else” is not made conditional. In a shared worktree, an agent that follows the leading absolute instruction and calls `ddflow_brief` with no identity first is the same failure mode previously described: identity is derived from the shared worktree, so the agent can receive another agent’s task and later review comparisons can bind to the wrong work. The rewrite moved the contradiction inside line 11 rather than resolving it; the earlier “SUPERSEDED” triage for the line-11/line-25 conflict therefore does not cover this new wording.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs that `ddflow_brief` "replaces reading this project's rule and lesson files — do not read those instead," but `ddflow_brief` is described as returning decisions that govern the files about to be touched and lessons ranked for the current task. The manual never restates the global advisory r-ddflow-self-assessment (assess ddflow at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction). An agent that obeys the manual's prohibition on reading the rule files has no remaining source for that required self-assessment and will omit it. This violates the advisory.

chunk_findings.detail: The compact text “One of several agents: `ddflow_identify` first, or `as_agent` on every call” makes `ddflow_identify` first an acceptable option on the stateless `2026-07-28` revision. On that revision there is no initialize connection, so `ddflow_identify` persists nothing; the old instructions explicitly said to name yourself on every call via `as_agent` or `_meta`. Given multiple agents in one worktree on that revision, an agent calls `ddflow_identify` once and stops; unlabeled later calls are derived from the working tree, identities merge, `ddflow_brief` can answer with someone else’s task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself and pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional loop “`ddflow_merge`, `ddflow_complete`” removes the PR integration branch. In a project with `[flow].integration = "pr"`, `ddflow_merge` opens the pull request, parks the item IN REVIEW, and releases the lease; the original contract said “do not wait and do not `ddflow_complete` it — take the next item.” The new charter tells that agent to call `ddflow_complete` on a parked item, producing a refusal/confusing loop exactly in the PR-flow case.

chunk_findings.detail: The "byte cap" is checked with `len(text)`, which counts Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes. The previous `mcp_instructions` pipeline line contained `" implement ·"` (U+00B7), so non-ASCII characters can make `len(text) <= 1500` while `len(text.encode()) > 1500`; the same issue is in the unadopted assertion at line 50 and the SessionStart assertion at line 75. Thus the cap this test is meant to enforce is not actually enforced.

chunk_findings.detail: After setting `gates.task_pipeline` to `implement,unit_tests,merge`, the test locates the `Gates:` line and only asserts that `rubber_duck` is absent. It no longer asserts that the configured gates appear, so a broken `_instructions` output such as `Gates: research · critic` passes both assertions. The test named `test_the_pipeline_shown_is_the_project_s_own` would fail to catch a regression that renders a different pipeline.

chunk_findings.detail: The pointer assertion is `assert "topic=manual" in _instructions(repo) or "manual" in _instructions(repo)`. Since `"manual"` is a substring of `"topic=manual"`, the second clause makes the first redundant and allows any mention of the word "manual" to satisfy the check. An instructions text like `"This is not a manual; call ddflow_help."` passes even though it never names the `manual` topic, so the test does not prove the charter points at the manual.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The first step still says “Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else” while in the same rewritten sentence says, for one of several agents/subagents, “name yourself first.” Those are two different first actions, and the absolute “before anything else” is not made conditional. In a shared worktree, an agent that follows the leading absolute instruction and calls `ddflow_brief` with no identity first is the same failure mode previously described: identity is derived from the shared worktree, so the agent can receive another agent’s task and later review comparisons can bind to the wrong work. chunk_findings.detail: The manual asserts “A plain `ddflow_review` of a gate with a recorded review is a full re-review”, but the same parenthetical states `full=true` is needed when `[review].delta_default` is on—meaning a plain `ddflow_review` is not a full re-review in that configuration. Under `[review].delta_default = true`, an agent following the broad statement will call plain `ddflow_review` expecting the whole diff; the tool actually performs a delta review only (full requires `full=true`), so the full diff is never re-reviewed and a gate can pass with unreviewed changes. The sentence must be qualified: plain is full only when `delta_default` is off; when it is on, plain is delta and `full=true` is required for a full review.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual authorizes an agent to resolve an un-made project flow choice without the operator: “ask the operator, or choose what suits the project with `ddflow_flow_choose` and a reason.” The contract this change is supposed to preserve is “ask the operator.” An agent that follows the “or choose” branch on a project-level branching-model/release-line decision can unilaterally set operator-owned policy with `ddflow_flow_choose`, bypassing the required operator decision.

chunk_findings.detail: The new comment asserts the injected charter is "<= 1.5K chars", but the same change's fresh-install test still allows a larger rendered `mcp_instructions` string: the triage records `FRESH_INIT_MAX` at 2300 bytes with a measured fresh output around 2208 bytes, and the comment itself says the shipped charter renders `setup_todo`. A freshly initialised project with every setup notice on therefore emits an injection well over the advertised 1500 characters (for the all-ASCII setup-sentence output, 2208 bytes is 2208 chars). A future edit that follows this comment can still pass the fresh-init test while producing output ~700 chars over the stated budget, so the cap claimed in the file is false for an actual agent-facing surface.

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement for the `gate_gaps` notice now instructs: `Gates with no tool behind them: ...; record `unavailable`, never imply a tool ran.` The deleted text explicitly preserved the case that some of those gates are direct agent judgement: “Several of those are judgement you do directly — that is fine and expected.” A project whose `gate_gaps` contains a direct-judgement gate such as `rubber_duck` will now tell the agent to record that gate `unavailable` instead of actually performing the gate. That skips a required quality gate on the record, which is the opposite of the previous, correct behavior.

The old `test_each_missing_companion_carries_its_install_command`, which asserted one `Install:` per missing companion, is deleted in this diff. A regression that makes `ddflow_companions` return a bare list of companion names with no install commands passes this new test, so the suite no longer enforces the exact “install command per companion” property its own docstring still states.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs the agent to "Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else" at line 11, then at line 25 instructs an agent in a multi-agent/subagent context to "call `ddflow_identify` first." These two first-step orders are mutually exclusive and the manual never states which one has precedence. In a multi-agent workspace, an agent that obeys line 11 calls `ddflow_brief` before `ddflow_identify`, contrary to the multi-agent-specific order the section itself says is required to avoid merging identities, receiving another agent's task, and a review gate comparing the agent against itself.

chunk_findings.detail: For `gate_gaps`, the new line says “Gates with no tool behind them: …; record `unavailable`, never imply a tool ran.” But `gate_gaps` contains gates the agent is expected to perform directly — the removed text explicitly said “Several of those are judgement you do directly — that is fine and expected.” Concrete input: a repository whose pipeline has `standards` but no codeguide-mcp installed, so `standards` appears in `gate_gaps`. Following the new instruction, the agent records `standards` as `unavailable` even after doing the manual standards review. That produces a false “could not run” result and discards the actual direct judgement/evidence. `unavailable` is for a tool or reviewer that could not run, not for a gate that has no external tool behind it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion `"context7" not in [c["id"] for c in vars_["actionable_companions"]]` verifies only the intermediate `_instruction_vars` decision, not the actual served instructions. The test then forcibly sets `vars_["actionable_companions"] = []` before rendering, so it never calls `_instructions(repo)` on the real repository state where `context7` is registered but `roborev`, `codeguide`, and `OptMem` are still missing. A production `_instructions` that correctly excludes `context7` from `_instruction_vars` but still renders a `"not wired up ... context7"` line via another variable or post-processing would pass this test, yet the actual served instructions would be wrong; the removed `test_a_registered_companion_is_not_listed_as_missing` covered that integration path and has not been replaced.
